The best part is that this audio series is still going strong at 70 episodes, with one released every month.

Star Trek: Excelsior, produced by James Heaney and Mike Hennessy) This series focuses on the USS Excelsior and its exploration of the Delta Quadrant via an Iconian gateway. Obstensively an exploration and diplomatic mission, not all is as it seems. The series is released in seasons, and better yet, the most recent fourth season is designed as a jumping off point for new listeners if you don't want to listen to the first three seasons.

Star Trek: Defiant, written and produced by Jeffrey Bridges One of the oldest productions on this list, Defiant began as fan fiction written through a mailing list in 1995. It concerns the 3rd commander of the Defiant, coincidentally named Jeffrey Bridges, and his crew. Unfortunately, in 2012, Bridges and his production company shut down all fan productions with intellectual property. You can find the episodes, but it's kind of hard. Message me if you need help. In any case, this series is included here because it relates to the next one.

Star Trek: The Section 31 Files, written and produced by Eric L. Busby The clandestine operations of Section 31 and their starship, the USS Nosferatu. Lots of stuff here. Features some crew from the aforementioned Defiant as they battle forces set to destroy the Federation or the universe. Busby has some fun with this as well, with occasional episodes featuring Doctor Who references and Star Wars crossovers, but all in all, a very well done show that is no longer being produced, and shows a side of the Federation that was not explored in depth. I used to listen to this all the time 10 years ago, and I would recommend it highly.

Star Trek: Lost Frontier, written and produced by Eric L. Busby Another production by Busby, this one takes places in the 25th century where a major disaster has left the Federation in pieces. The USS Enterprise-F is tasked with bringing the old worlds of the Federation together to create a new union.
